title: Boilerplate, dickered terms, and the battle of forms
shortTitle: Boilerplate, dickered terms, and the battle of forms
summary: Routine commercial forms can agree on the transaction while conflict remains in their standard clauses.
notes: The casebook draws on Macaulay’s account of quotations, purchase orders, and acknowledgments. Operating personnel may check item, quantity, price, and delivery while overlooking terms drafted by lawyers or copied from other forms. This explains why section 2-207 recognizes contracts despite some differences. It does not eliminate the need for a definite expression of acceptance or make radical changes to the commercial terms irrelevant.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 272–276. Open assigned page 272.
